rows.author: C128
rows.abstract: REP. PAEZ TOOK THE FLOOR ON BEHALF OF THE MARGINAL FISHERFOLKS AND FISH VENDORS IN PARANAQUE CITY WHO ARE FACING THREAT OF EVICTION BY THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT FROM THE PARANAQUE FISHERMAN'S WHARF, AND WHICH WAS ESTABLISHED AS A FISH TERMINAL...; INFORMED THE BODY THAT HE WOULD FILE A RESOLUTION URGING THE CTTEE. ON COOPERATIVES DEV'T TO CONDUCT AN INQUIRY... ON THE REASONS WHY THEY WERE NOT ACCORDED THE APPROPRIATE JUST COMPENSATION AND WHY THE PARCEL OF RECLAIMED GOV'T LAND HAS NOT BEEN AWARDED TO THEM.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2012-05-28
rows.remarks: Interpellation and Manifestation by Rep. Olivares.

rows.author: G088
rows.abstract: FOCUSED ON THE IMPLICATIONS OF THE RECENTLY ISSUED COMELEC RESO. 9374 WHICH DISCONTINUED ACTION AND EFFECTIVELY DENIED ALL PETITIONS FOR THE CONDUCT OF RECALL ELECTIONS DUE TO BUDGETARY CONSTRAINTS AND TEDIOUS ELECTION PREPARATIONS; SAID THAT MECHANISMS OF RECALL UNDER THE LGC HAVE BEE PROVEN INEFFECTIVE AND EVEN INIMICAL TO THE COMMON GOOD; INFORMED THE BODY THAT HE FILED A BILL REPEALING THE ENTIRE PROVISION ON \"RECALL\"...
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2012-05-28

rows.author: F102
rows.title_full: SAVING PHILIPPINE FISHERIES RESOURCES AND EMPOWERING FISHERFOLKS
rows.abstract: REP. BELLO SPOKE ON THE CRISIS IN THE FISHERIES AND AQUATIC SECTOR WHERE 1.5 MILLION MEN AND WOMEN IN THE FISHERFOLK COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE COUNTRY ARE BEING THREATENED BY THE PREVALENCE OF FISHPONDS AND AQUACULTURE PRODUCTION, CLIMATE CHANGE AND FISH IMPORTATION; STATED THAT THE GOVERNMENT SHOULD ENSURE THE RIGHTS AND WELFARE OF THE FISHERFOLK... AND PRIORITIZE THE PARTICIPATION OF LOCAL FISHING COMMUNITIES IN THE MANAGEMENT OF MARINE AND AQUATIC RESOURCES; URGED THE GOV'T, IN SOLIDARITY WITH THE SAVE THE FISHERIES NOW NETWORK TO TAKE SEVERAL STEPS TO ENSURE THE REHABILITATION OF THE FISHERIES SECTOR AND THE PROTECTION OF THE LIVES AND LIVELIHOOD OF THE FILIPINO FISHERFOLK.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AQUACULTURE AND FISHERIES RESOURCES since 2012-07-24

rows.author: G012
rows.title_full: BAYBAYIN: WIKANG PANULAT SA TINUBUANG LUPA
rows.abstract: SPOKE ABOUT THE NEED TO PROTECT AND CONSERVE BAYBAYIN AND TO RECOGNIZE THE IMPORTANCE OF WRITING IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND PRESERVATION OF CIVILIZATION;... SAID THAT HE AUTHORED HB 2011 DECLARING BAYBAYIN AS THE NATIONAL SCRIPT. STRESSED THAT THE COUNTRY SHOULD HAVE ITS OWN SYSTEM OF WRITING TO ALLOW IT TO COMPETE WITH THE PROGRESSIVE ASIAN AND MIDDLE EAST NATIONS WHICH HAVE THEIR OWN STYLE OF WRITING.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2012-07-24
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Reps. Rodriguez(R.)and Padilla. Referred to the Committee on Basic Education and Culture.

rows.author: A010
rows.title_full: PLUNDER OF THE QUEDANCOR SWINE PROGRAM FUNDS
rows.abstract: REP. AUMENTADO DENOUNCED THE PLUNDER OF FUNDS FOR THE QUEDANCOR SWINE PROGRAM (QSP) IMPLEMENTED BY THE QUEDANCOR-ILOILO DISTRICT OFFICE AND THE USE OF HIS NAME BY UNSCRUPULOUS AND CRIMINAL ELEMENTS IN REGARD THERETO...DETAILED HOW THE SAID OFFICE ACCREDITED BIRKS AGRICULTURAL-LIVESTOCK CORPORATION AS THE SOLE INPUT SUPPLIER FOR THE PROGRAM... STRESSED THAT QSP MANAGEMENT COMMITTED FRAUDULENT ACTS THAT COA SHOULD HAVE FIRST LOOKED INTO TO ASCERTAIN THE INVOLVEMENT OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS. ASKED THE HOUSE CTTEES. ON GOOD GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY TO INQUIRE INTO THE SCAM AND ON REMEDIAL MEASURES TO PREVENT ITS REPEAT AND TO INDORSE HIS REQUEST FOR AN NBI INVESTIGATION.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOOD GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY since 2012-07-24

rows.author: F102
rows.title_full: UPHOLDING OF JUSTICE AND HUMAN RIGHTS FOR COCOY TULAWIE
rows.abstract: REP. BELLO URGED THE BODY TO STAND BY THE RIGHTS ESPECIALLY TO A SPEEDY AND IMPARTIAL TRIAL, OF MR. TEMOGEN \"COCOY\" TULAWIE WHOM HE REFERRED TO AS THE SYMBOL OF HUMAN RIGHTS IN SULU...HE ADDED THAT IN 2009, MR. TULAWIE WAS CHARGED WITH MULTIPLE FRUSTRATED MURDER FOR A BOMBING INCIDENT THAT INJURED SEVERAL PEOPLE INCLUDING THE GOVERNOR. SUBSEQUENTLY, REP. BELLO STRESSED THE NEED TO DEFEND THE RIGHTS OF MANY OTHER HUMAN RIGHTS ADVOCATES WHO CONTINUE TO LANGUISH IN JAIL AND TO CONDEMN THE GROWING GLOBAL TREND OF REPRESSION AND CRIMINALIZATION OF THE DEFENDERS OF THE POOR, THE MARGINALIZED AND THE POWERLESS.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HUMAN RIGHTS since 2012-07-24

rows.author: G085
rows.title_full: EXPRESSED GRATITUDE TO THE UN FOR HIS APPOINTMENT AS A MEMBER OF THE UNITED NATIONS INTERNATIONAL STRATEGY FOR DISASTER REDUCTION (UNISRD)
rows.abstract: REP. SARMIENTO (M.)INFORMED THE BODY OF HIS APPOINTMENT AS A MEMBER OF THE UNITED NATIONS SECRETARIAT OF THE INTERNATIONAL STRATEGY FOR DISASTER RISK REDUCTION (UNISDR) ADVISORY GROUP OF PARLIMANETARIANS.  HE EXPLAINED THE GOAL OF THE BODY, WHICH IS TO ENSURE THE BUILDING OF DISASTER RESILIENT COMMUNITIES.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2012-07-24

rows.author: E047
rows.title_full: ALLEGED MILITARIZATION AND VIOLATION OF HUMAN RIGHTS IN THE SOUTHERN TAGALOG REGION
rows.title_short: Militarization In The Province Of Quezon
rows.abstract: REP. MARIANO CONDEMNED THE MILITARIZATION OF THE DISTRICTS OF TIMOG QUEZON AND BONDOC PENINSULA IN QUEZON PROVINCE AS A RESULT OF THE IMPLEMENTATION OF OPLAN BANTAY LAYA AND OPLAN BAYANIHAN OF THE AFP... HE CITED STATISTICS RE: HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS...STRESSED THAT THE INTEREST OF MARGINALIZED SECTORS FIGHTING AGAINST LANDGRABING AND LAND CONVERSION CONFLICTED WITH THOSE OF PUBLIC AND PRIVATE GROUPS WHO WANTED TO DEVELOP THE AREA COMMERCIALLY. STRESSED THAT THE GOVERNMENT SHOULD PULL OUT THE EIGHT BATALLIONS OF SOLDIERS AND SPECIAL FORCES THEREAT AND IMMEDIATELY CONDUCT AN INVESTIGATION THEREON.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HUMAN RIGHTS since 2012-07-24

rows.author: F100
rows.title_full: UNCONSTITUTIONAL AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE PNOC AND OIL COMPANIES SHELL AND CHEVRON ON THE MALAMPAYA PROJECT
rows.abstract: Rep.Colmenares talked about the misuse of the Malampaya funds as well as the illegality and unconstitutionality of what he described as a disadvantageous agreement between the Phil. government represented by the PNOC and the big oil cos. represented by Shell and Chevron; urged the Body to investigate the negotiations for said contracts esp. as the government was bent on extending them; the anomalies involved therein; and the public officials who have squandered or intend to squander public resources; suggested the giving of service contracts to Filipino-owned corporations rather than transnationals...
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2012-07-24

rows.title_full: HOUSING PROGRAMS FOR THE UNDERPRIVILEGED
rows.abstract: Rep. Rodolfo G. Valencia sought ...support for the bill creating a Department of Housing, Planning and Urban Dev't out of the HUDCC;...explained that the agency would ensure increased and sustained shelter delivery and continuing urban development in acc. with the provisions of the 1987 Constitution and several housing laws;... emphasized that housing was a universally recognized pump-primer of the economy and that many other countries... had their own Housing Departments.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT since 2012-07-24

rows.author: A076
rows.title_short: Report On The S O N A
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2012-07-25)

rows.author: G009
rows.title_full: ARMS TRADE
rows.abstract: Rep. Bag-ao argued against the proliferation of firearms...to end humanitarian and human rights abuses and achieve a more peaceful world. Against the backdrop of the failure of over170 countries to reach an agreement re: an Arms Trade Treaty during the recent UN Diplomatic Conference, she claimed that the Phils. has more at stake in the ratification of such treaty...(enumerated the ill effects of loose firearms/arms proliferation; urged Congress to support a global standard for the arms trade and the \"no arms for atrocities\" principle...; enumerated several recommendations to Congress...
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2012-08-13
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Biazon, Golez (R.). Referred to Rules.

rows.author: G085
rows.title_full: TRANSFORMING THE CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION (CSC)
rows.abstract: Rep. Sarmiento cited the compliance by the CSC with the requisites of a PGS hinged on the balance scoreboard technology, a performance management tracking tool...; explained that CSC intended to be more responsive and transparent...in close partnership with the private sector; discussed the CSC's accomplishments...; advocated the use of the PGS in other government agencies.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2012-08-13

rows.author: E047
rows.title_full: INCREASING PRICES OF OIL, ELECTRICITY, WATER AND OTHER UTILITIES
rows.title_short: Power, Water And Oil Price Increase
rows.abstract: Rep. Mariano called the attention of the Body on the recent spate of eletric, water and oil price increases... which he said is caused by the implementation of the EPIRA, the privatization of water utilities and the penchant of private cos. to accumulate huge profits. Rep. Mariano reiterated the demand... for the repeal of the EPIRA and the legislation of an across-the-board P125 minimum wage increase, called on the DOE, and DTI to immediately implement a freeze on the prices of oil and basic commodities and services, and enjoined the Members to immediately act and take the necessary steps towards solving the problem.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECONOMIC AFFAIRS since 2012-08-13

rows.author: F104
rows.title_full: DEATH OF MARC ANDRE MARCOS ALLEGEDLY DUE TO HAZING
rows.abstract: Rep. Palatino spoke on...fraternity-related violence which allegedly took the life of a freshman law student from San Beda College...; recalled that ...Congress passsed the Anti-Hazing Law in light of the death of a law freshman from Ateneo de Manila due to fraternity hazing. He said that he had filed House Resolution No. 2188... to review...the exclusion of community fraternities and sororities from the mandate of the law and the exemption of hazing activities perpetrated by the military and police training institutions from its coverage...; pointed out that the challenge at hand...to enact laws and create projects that would enable the creation of a culture of collective action which would empower the youth to contribute to the resolution of society's more relevant and pressing issues.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2012-08-13
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Socrates.  Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: E022
rows.title_short: Plight Of O F W S In Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
rows.abstract: Rep. Casino called the attention of the Body to the plight of the 194 OFWs based in the KSA who, out of desperation, have left their work places and went on hunger strike due to illegal recruitment practices and contract violations as well as the indifference and inefficiency of the Phil. Embassy officials to act on their conditions;... After noting the DFA'S meager budget for the OFWs despite the billions of dollars which they contribute to the country's economy, he then urged the government to address the problems caused by the country's labor export program, specifically calling for an immediate action on the case of the 194 OFWs.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2012-08-06)

rows.author: G068
rows.title_full: \"IT'S TIME TO CHA CHA!\"
rows.abstract: Rep. Panotes...expressed support to the proposal to revisit the 1987 Constitution, and commended Spkr. Feliciano Belmonte Jr. for asserting the agenda on Charter change (Chacha) to allow sweeping reform in its economic provisions; noted that significant strides in rebuilding the nation were not enough to alleviate poverty and improve the lives of the people, and recommended amendments to the constitutional provisions on national economy; urged Congress to continuously exert efforts to uphold the rights of the Filipinos, protect the national sovereignty, defend the nation's assets against unfair practices and unscrupulous use by industry players, and guarantee reciprocity aginst foreign investments; agreed with the Speaker's view that changing the Charter... will allow a thorough appreciation of all arguments and produce the finest fusion of insights, foresights and discussion on the issues at hand; spare the country from another grueling struggle; and save the government from divisive politics and excessive spending.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENTS since 2012-08-15
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Ocampos. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: A040
rows.title_full: S O L A R  P O W E R
rows.abstract: Rep.Golez spoke about the emerging world of solar power, initially citing several studies that dwelt on the potential of solar energy to cost lower than fossil fuel energy in the future and on the recent increase in investments by developed countries...But despite the low feed-in tariff rate approval for solar power generation by the DOE, he disclosed that the local arm of a Belgian renewable energy developer has committed to push through with its planned solar power portfolio in the Philippines; explained to the Body, how solar energy works; the applications of renewable solar energy systems...; cited several articles which report the success stories of solar energy in various part of the world...; discussed the significant developments in solar energy research which allowed for a more efficient use of solar energy in solar-powered vehicles and energized residences...
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2012-08-15
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Salimbangon and Padilla. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: E022
rows.title_short: Worsening Weather Problems Due To Climate Change
rows.abstract: Cited the recent damage to life and property caused by heavy rains as a result of climate change and stressed that the Phils. ranked 3rd in the list of countries with highest risk against climate change; suggested a strategy to mitigate if not stop the problem by reducing carbon dioxide emission: shift the diet of the citizenry from a meat-based to a vegetable-based one because the livestock industry was a major contributor to environmental pollution; informed the Body that Sofia School in Meycauayan, Bulacan was already implementing a \"meat-less Monday\" or \"Luntiang Lunes\" campaign...; added that he had filed the \"Luntiang Lunes Bill and asked his colleagues to heed the clamor of the youth.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2012-08-13)

rows.author: F102
rows.title_full: EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE
rows.abstract: Rep. Bello delved on the need for an international action on climate change...; quoted the Secretary of the DENR as saying that the climate has become unpredictable due to the uncontrolled rise in global temperature caused by green-house gas emissions...; showed how developed countries...are the ones that have contributed more than half of the greenhouse gases in the atmosphere... were also the ones most difficult to deal seriously with global warming; related how the so-called North_South dimension ahs added a deadly dynamic to the process and how the emerging capitalist economies of the South... have made claims to their share of ecological space to grow even as the economies of the North have continued to refuse to give up any space they now occupy and exploit; explained that countries like the Phils., which are most threatened by climate change, should do all it can to break the deadlock caused by the refusal of the North to curb their high consumption and the effort of big emerging economies to reproduce the northern consumption model by engaging in \"anti-diplomacy\"; enumerate the coalitions among developing countries which should push for an agenda separate from that of the Group of && and China as well as the North.; said that the Aquino Administration must commit to reduce the country's greenhouse gas emissions... and this would mean shelving the fossil fuel energies as well as plans to set up a national network of coal-generated power plants; concluded that when diplomacy fails, the country ahs no choice but to resort to strategies like anti-diplomacy and moral suasion to safeguard the national security and interest.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2012-08-15

rows.author: F095
rows.title_full: AMBUSH OF DR. REYES OF LIPA, BATANGAS
rows.abstract:
Rep. Briones called attention to an ambush...
that resulted to the death of the brother-in-law of his constituent and leader Dr. Ernesto Reyes; said that both he & Dr. Reyes had been advocating for the change of registration of Batelec II from the NEDA to the Cooperative Development Authority (CDA) to maximize the benefits of its members and to resolve the issue on the election of its board of directors; urged Congress to look into the operations of electric cooperatives esp. the conversion of their registration from the NEA to CDA; and for the PNP to immediately investigate the ambush case of Dr. Reyes and impose the full force of the law to resolve the case.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2012-08-15

rows.author: G120
rows.title_full: DISCRIMINATORY PRACTICES IMPOSED BY PILAR COLLEGE AND UNIVERSIDAD DE ZAMBOANGA TOWARDS THEIR MUSLIM STUDENTS
rows.title_short: Discrimination Of Muslim Women Students At The Pilar College And Universidad De Zamboanga
rows.abstract: Rep. Pangandaman M. called the attention of the Body...where Muslim women students are prohibited from wearing their traditional hijab or niqab within the school premises; lamented that the actuation ... is irresponsible considering that the Constitution guarantees religious freedom; stated that even as the Zamboanga City council has already passed a resolution questioning said policy..., the latter has stood firm in its decision; asked why religious dicrimination still persists in the 21st century and called for the right to practice religion to become a paramount principle for all Filipinos because all men are created equal.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2012-08-29
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Rep. Climaco. Interpellation by Rep. Rodriguez(R)- inquired on the alleged refusal by apartment and dormitory owners particularly those surrounding Xavier University in Cagayan de Oro City to admit Muslim students... Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F087
rows.title_full: HIGH POWER RATES IN BANTAYAN ISLAND, CEBU
rows.title_short: Very High Power Rates That Will Be Imposed To Bantayan Island
rows.abstract: Rep. Salimbangon delved on the impending increase in power rates in Bantayan Island, Cebu... due to the decision of the NPC to withhold its subsidy to the Bantayan Island Power Corp. which supplies energy to the island's Bantayan Electric Cooperative; urged the Body to request the NPC to reconsider the withholding of the subsidy and to ask the NPC, the DOE and the ERC to look into the matter very seriously as welll as suspend the implementation of the power rate increase.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2012-08-29

rows.author: A040
rows.title_short: Effects Of The \"habagat\" And The Coming Typhoon
rows.abstract: Rep. Golez cited statistics and also presented pictures and video presentation on the magnitude of the damage to life and property caused by the heavy rains in Metro Manila and nearby provinces...; recalled that when Typhoon Ondoy struck the country..., Congress soon approved a Joint Resolution authorizing the allocation of funds for the relief operations as well as rehabilitation and reconstruction of affected areas damaged by said typhoon;...observed that when the recent calamity occurred, the House did not address the problem but instead debated on the RH Bill...; thanked Rep. Gabriela for prioritizing the flood victims over and above its other endeavors and advocacy; referred to the assurance of Sen. Franklin Drilon..., that Congress would approved more flood funds, ...; lamented that the House has not done anything to reciprocate the Senate's concern... despite the fact that many Members of the House represent the affected areas.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2012-08-15)

rows.author: F057
rows.title_full: NON-PAYMENT OF OVERTIME SERVICES RENDERED BY OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES OF THE BUREAU OF IMMIGRATION
rows.title_short: Government's Preferential Option For Just Compensation Of Gov't Employees
rows.abstract: Rep. Rodriguez spoke on the encroachment by the Executive Dept. on the right of Congress to decide on the payment of overtime work rendered by public customs, immigration and quarantine (CIQ) employees, specifically citing the memoranda... which in effect favor airline cos. to stop paying CIQ employees the overtime pay due them; underscored how laws...justify the collection by public CIQ employees of overtime pay from airline and shipping cos., importers and shippers; stressed that the Finance Secretary's suggestion of allowing the gov't to shoulder the overtime pay would lessen the country's dwindling resources and in effect burden the taxpayers with the payment; maintained that the recent suspension by the two Departments of overtime pay collection for services rendered by gov't CIQ employees in the NAIA was an unlawful encroachment on the powers vested by C.A.No. 613 to the Immigration Commissioner...
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2012-09-04
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Lagman, Magsaysay (M.), Romualdo, Casino and Bichara. Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: F118
rows.title_full: COMMEMORATION OF THE INOPACAN MASSACRE (6TH ANNIVERSARY)
rows.title_short: Exhumation Of 67 Human Skeletal Remains On August 28, 2006
rows.abstract: Rep. Alcover, Jr...said that it was the 6th year anniversary of the discovery of a mass grave in Inopacan, Leyte; denounced the atrocity committed by the Maoist CPP-NPA...; lamented that the gov't failed to perform its duty to ferret out the truth and bring justice to the families of the victims...; expressed belief that justice is still nowhere in sight as the gov't has been manipulated, exploited and abused as shown by its leniency and tolerance to the inhumanity and violence perpetrated with impunity by the members of the CPP-NPA-NDF...
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PEACE, RECONCILIATION AND UNITY since 2012-09-04

rows.author: A024
rows.title_full: PEACE AND ORDER SITUATION IN MINDANAO
rows.title_short: Outbreak Of Violence In The Municipalities Of Maguindanao
rows.abstract: Rep. Simeon A Datumanong denounced the simultaneous attacks staged during Ramadan by members of the Bangsamoro Islamic Freedom Movement (BIFM)... against military detachments and civilian centers in the municipalities...all located in the 2nd District of Maguindanao; proposed the conduct of an investgiation on the alleged involvement and support of some public officials in Maguindanao on these attacks; the brazenness of the attacks...; and, the effects of thses hostilities on the ongoing peace negotiations etween the government and the MILF; urged the national gov't to further investigate and validate the reports so that appropriate sanctions may be imposed upon the responsible officials; asked the Cttee. on Peace and Reconciliation to investigate... said incidents.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PEACE, RECONCILIATION AND UNITY since 2012-09-04
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Biazon. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.title_full: INADEQUACIES AND LAPSES OF THE C A A P
rows.title_short: C A A P's Shortcomings In The Implementation Of Its Obligation
rows.abstract: Citing aircraft accidents such as that involving the late DILG Sec. Jesse Robredo, Rep. Fua enumerated the shortcomings of both the DOTC and Civil Aviation Authority of the Phils.(CAAP) for rescue and retrieval operations; urged the agencies... to adopt remedial measures...
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2012-09-04

rows.author: G067
rows.title_full: TAAL LAKE REHABILITATION
rows.title_short: Protection, Conservation And Preservaton Of Taal Lake
rows.abstract: Rep. Angelo B. Palmones asked for his colleagues' support for the protection, conservation and preservation of the Taal Volcano Protected Landscape (TVPL) as well as the Taal Lake... Citing the needed safeguards for the protection of said areas, he mentioned the ff.: 1) laws and regulations such as Pres'l Proc. No. 906 creating the TVPL, the 1992 Nat'l Integrated Protected Areas System (NIPAS) Act and the Clean Water Act; 2) action by the DENR including the dismantling of fish pens and cages, inventorying piggeries and restaurants, allotment of addit'l rehabilitation funds, and conducting clean-up drives; 3) filing of petitions ... aimed at monitoring compliance with the aforecited laws, water quality, status of fish cages, and the like; and 4) his filing of HB 6156 ... creation of the position of Protected Area Superintendent (PASu) in each NIPAS area.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2012-09-04

rows.author: C128
rows.title_full: Rep. Cresente C. Paez...spoke about the alarming situation in the Davao del Norte Electric Cooperative (Daneco) which was operating with two sets of directors, general managers, employees, and collection groups; stressed that the Cooperative Dev't Authority (CDA) is the sole gov't body mandated to promote the viability and growth of cooperatives...but noted severa blatant attempts of the NEA to abort the registration of the Daneco with the CDA and its possible conversion into a stock cooperative; denounced the continuous control and manipulation by the NEA of the said electric cooperative; stated that he filed a Resolution ...on the matter and urged the gov't agencies concerned to let electric cooperatives grow and realize their full potentials...
rows.title_short: Interference Of N E A And Its Authority Over D A N E C O
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2012-09-03)
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Ping-ay, Padilla, Magsaysay (M.), Rivera, Briones and Salimbangon. Manifestation by Rep. Teves.

rows.author: G093
rows.title_full: PASSAGE OF MEASURES PROVIDING ADDITIONAL BENEFITS TO PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS
rows.title_short: Commemoration Of Teacher's Month / Rights And Welfare Of Teachers
rows.abstract: Rep. Tinio talked about the commemoration of the National Teacher's Month...with the celebration of World Teachers' Day in view of the unique role and service of teachers in educating children; opined that the most meaningful and sincere expression of gratitude for teachers is by giving full effect to their rights to a living salary, adequate remuneration, stability of employment, union rights, among others; said that the proposed DepEd budget for 2013 has no allotment for salary increases for teachers; and that certain Executive issuances banned the increase in existing bonuses or grant of new ones despite a P9-billion allotment for a system of performance-based bonuses; urged the Executive to review its policies; asked the Legislature to pass pro-teacher measures such as HBs 2142 and 3746 as he remarked that it had already approved on Third Reading HB 4097, declaring Oct. 5 of every year as National Teacher's Day.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2012-12-05
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules on Sept. 04, 2012.

rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2012-09-18)

rows.author: G057
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2012-09-18)

rows.author: F115
rows.title_full: PASSAGE OF MEASURES PROVIDING ADDITIONAL BENEFITS TO SENIOR CITIZENS
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2012-12-05

rows.author: G050
rows.title_full: ALLEGATIONS AGAINST HIM REGARDING THE \"TULAY NG PANGULO\"
rows.abstract: Rep. Haresco took the floor to answer the allegations of corruption cited by an incumbent Senator... re: the 18-year old Tulay ng Pangulo or President's Bridge Program ...; clarified that 1) the Office of the Ombudsman already dismissed ... all allegations filed in connection with the program; 2) even the UK House of Commons cleared the Philippines of any incident of bribery or anomaly...;3)COA reported that the program incurred no cost overruns; and 4)the cross-border currency denomination was proven advantageous to the Philippines; He also criticized the Senator for working against the betterment of the Province of Aklan and its people, and for using what he termed as unparliamentary, gestapo tactics to get information about his personal and professiona life to malign him...; urged his colleagues to investigate Balfour Beatty's poor contract performance and cost overruns to be able to identify its politician-protector.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2012-12-05
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules on October 8, 2012.

rows.author: F076
rows.title_full: ILLEGAL MINING ACTIVITIES IN CARRANGLAN, NUEVA ECIJA
rows.abstract: Rep. Violago called on the DENR and all other government agencies tasked in implementing environmental laws to immediately halt illegal mining operations in Carranglan, Nueva Ecija...; referred in particular... the termination of illegal mining activities in Sitio Binbin, Bgy. Gen. Luna, Carranglan but which the DENR has not acted upon,...; appealed for the implementation of the NIPAS Act of 1992 and then asked for his colleagues' support to his case.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2012-12-05
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Padilla and Bello. Referred to the Committee on Rules on October 08, 2012.

rows.author: G108
rows.title_full: PASSAGE OF ANTI-GRAFT AND CORRUPTION MEASURES
rows.abstract: Rep. Tugna...focused his speech on how to eradicate and prevent graft and corruption using...holistic approach...; underscored that the fight against graft and corruption must not be compartmentalized... everyone must take part in such endeavor by being aware of their rights and responsibilities as citizens of the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2012-12-05
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules on October 08, 2012.

Runrono in Nueva Vizcaya, wherein the workers of the FCF Minerals Corp...injured some of the residents there; sought the assistance of the House leadership...

rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G008
rows.title_full: EXPRESSED GRATITUDE OF CONGRESS AND VARIOUS GOVERNMENT AGENCIES FOR THE FINANCIAL AID TO THE VICTIMS OF TYPHOON \"PABLO\" AND SOUGHT CONTINUING ASSISTANCE
rows.title_short: Typhoon \" P A B L O \"
rows.abstract:
Rep. Zamora spoke about the untold misery and
devastation that Typhoon Pablo brought to the
people, economy, and environment of the First
District of Compostela Valley. She also expressed
her continuing appeal for assistance and compassion for the typhoon victims even as she thanked, among others, the Office of the President for mapping out strategies for the rebuilding and rehabilitation of the province;...
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2013-01-22

rows.author: G059
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR INVESTIGATION ON OFFICIALS OF D O L E REGION IV - A
rows.title_short: Investigation On Some D O L E Officials At Region Iv - A
rows.abstract:
Rep. Loyola focused on the several incidents of
disrespect which he received from certain officials of DOLE in the course of the actions and inquiries he had conducted to address the alleged inefficiencies of acting Regional Director Alex Avila and acting Asst. Regional Director Mila Mata of DOLE Region IV-A. ...He thereafter asked his colleagues to investigate the said officials of DOLE Region IV-A, specifically their alleged neglect of their sworn duties, their malversation of public funds,
and their promotion to higher ranks despite their
involvement in certain anomalies.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOOD GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY since 2013-01-22

rows.author: E047
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR GENUINE LAND REFORM
rows.title_short: 26th Year Annivesary Of Mendiola Massacre / Genuine Agrarian Reform
rows.abstract:
Rep. Rafael V. Marian.. urged Congress to immediately enact House Bill No. 374 or the Genuine Agrarian Reform Bill (GARB) into law
to give justice to the victims of the 13
farmers who died during the Mendiola Massacre on
January 22, 1987 as well as to address the
demand of the Filipino peasants for a true land
reform. He said that the measure will solve the
following problems which the CARP and the CARPER laws have failed to address: the hundred-year old problems of peasants and farmers on lack of land distribution; poverty; land monopoly by landlords and foreigners; and true and lasting peace throughout the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRARIAN REFORM since 2013-01-22
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Apostol and Fua.  Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: E022
rows.title_full: IMPLEMENTATION BY THE DOTC-LTO OF A DEPARTMENT ORDER ON INCREASE IN FINES AND PENALTIES FOR TRAFFIC VIOLATIONS AND OTHER VIOLATIONS
rows.title_short: Increase On Fines, Charges And Penalties On Public Land Transportation
rows.abstract:
Rep. Teddy A. Casiño urged the House to address the continued dillydallying by the DOTC and LTO to stop implementing DOTC Department Order (DO) No. 2008-39 which arbitrarily revised the schedule of fines and penalties for traffic and administrative violations. He stressed that the courts had ruled that the DO was unconstitutional because it is the Legislature and not the Executive which enjoys the power of
taxation. He explained that the department order
increased among other things, fines and penalties for traffic violations as well as licensing and other fees; and that public utility drivers and operators considered it a scourge in addition to the abuses they
suffered from corrupt traffic enforcers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2013-01-22

rows.author: F069
rows.abstract:
Rep. Sy-Alvarado, ... emphasized that the province of Bulacan holds the singular and enviable distinction of being the cradle of the first three Republics that ever rose in Asia and Africa; narrated the historic events leading to Emilio Aguinaldo´s proclamation of Philippine Independence in Kawit, Cavite on June 12, 1898; underscored that June 12 and January 23 are inseparable in the same manner that Kawit and Malolos are the two ends that marked the starting point and the finish line of the country´s journey to nationhood....; stressed that the nation should commemorate January
23 not only in Bulacan but in the entire country to acknowledge the masses who bravely and
unceasingly fought for the country´s freedom. This would remind the nation, she continued, that freedom was attained because of united effort but was lost when it was left to the hands of a few; and that its continuous preservation should be the duty of every
citizen; ended her speech by asking support for House Bill No. 5762, declaring January 23 of every year as a national nonworking holiday.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-01-23)

rows.author: G093
rows.title_short: Violation Of The Tubattaha Law By The U S S Guardian
rows.abstract:
Rep. Tinio asked why authorities had not yet
filed any case against the US Government when its
minesweeper, the USS Guardian, recently went
aground the Tubbataha Reef; pointed out that the reef had been harmed and the Tubbataha Reef Natural Park Act of 2009 and Visiting Forces Agreement (VFA) had been violated; stressed that the Aquino Administration should implement the laws of the country and file charges against the commander and personnel of the USS Guardian as well as protect and defend the country´s
natural resources and national sovereignty
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-01-23)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Golez R., Farinas and Marcoleta. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: A040
rows.abstract:
Rep. Golez centered on the country´s claim on
the West Philippine Sea and expressed his pleasure over the adoption of House Resolution No. 3004, supporting the move of the Executive branch to file a Notification and Statement of Claim on the West Philippine Sea; stated for the record the statement made by the DFA in filing the said Notification which initiates the arbitral proceedings against China on the nine-dash line; stressed that his condemnation of
China´s incursion in the Mischief Reef or
Scarborough Shoal has been part of his advocacies
since his second term during the Tenth Congress;
thereafter cited several questions and answers
provided by the DFA as guidelines in his explanation of the consequences and significance of the filing of the Notification and Statement of Claim on the West Philippine Sea; expressed his strong support for H.R. No. 3004, and manifested that he had likewise filed H.R. No. 3005 in support thereof.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-01-23)

rows.author: B006
rows.title_short: M I L F Government Framework Peace Agreement
rows.abstract:
Rep. Balindong talked about the progress of the
ongoing peace talks between the Philippine
government and the MILF which resulted in the forging of the historic 2012 Framework Agreement on the Bangsamoro thus bringing a step closer to the creation of a new Bangsamoro Self-Governing Region to replace the present ARMM;...urged Congress to take a more proactive role in the
peace process;... recommended that the House
adopt the ff. institutional reforms: 1) the
conversion of the House Special Cttee. on
Peace, Reconciliation and Unity into a standing
committee with appropriate support; and 2) the
creation under said Committee of a Special
Subcommittee on the Mindanao Peace Process solely
devoted to all matters relating to the peace process in Mindanao...; provide linkages and effective mechanisms for consultation and collaboration; include the chairpersons of the
Cttees. on Constitutional Amendments and Muslim and Mindanao Affairs in its membership;
and be given adequate funding by Congress.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-01-28)

rows.author: G053
rows.title_short: Questionable Integrity Of Police Superintendent Reyanaldo Maclang
rows.abstract: Rep. Jalosjos decried the human rights violations and grave abuse of authority allegedly committed by Zamboanga del Norte Provincial Public Safety Commander Reynaldo Maclang, including the buybust operations and incarceration of media men; and his promotion by the DILG Sec. Mar Roxas despite the same...; questioned the integrity and capability of Secretary Roxas and asked whether he planned to demolish some provinces including Zamboanga del Norte because they were thorns in his political ambition.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-01-28)

rows.author: F102
rows.abstract:
Rep. Walden S. Bello... stated that even if the 15th Congress will be remembered in history as one of the most productive in terms of legislating bills that promote human and
democratic rights, there remains a vacuum when it
comes to bills that promote transparency and
democracy in the political process....then presented his arguments for the immediate passage of the Freedom of Information (FOI) Bill which he deems a necessary step towards the attainment of a more mature and democratic, and stronger Philippine republic.;...appealed to the Body to begin the discussion on the FOI Bill...
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-01-28)

rows.author: F040
rows.title_short: Rule Of Law And Good Governance
rows.abstract:
Rep. Labadlabad spoke on the present state of
governance and the rule of law in his province
concerning the implementation of a Supreme
Court decision by the DILG so it can cause the
arrest of, and enforce the jail sentence on Mayor
Dominador Jalosjos Jr. and install Mr. Agapito J.
Cardino as the newly proclaimed Mayor of Dapitan City.; stated that the DILG´s faithful adherence to the rule of law may have caused the emotional
outburst of Rep. Seth P. Jalosjos who had
insinuated that martial law was being exercised in the province and that human rights violations and grave abuse of authority were allegedly committed by Zamboanga del Norte Provincial Public Safety Commander Reynaldo Maclang.; said that there is absolutely no basis for blaming and
crucifying the DILG leadership for the alleged
malfeasance of Commander Maclang who was just
dutifully conducting and performing his official
duties. On the accusation that Sindangan has become the center of extrajudicial killings by Supt. Maclang, he maintained that it was an outrageous lie, and emphasized that the shooting incidents happened before the return of Supt. Maclang to Zamboanga del Norte...
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-01-30)

rows.author: G067
rows.title_short: Infestation Of Coconut Trees In Batangas By The Scale Insect
rows.abstract:
Rep. Palmones ...restate his concern for the coconut farmers of Batangas and its surrounding
provinces because of the scale insect infestation
attacking coconut trees in the said localities.
;... recalled the response of the Phil. Coconut Authority (PCA) to his call for an immediate inquiry and action under H.R.No. 2112, the
allocation by his Party-List Agham of funds out of PDAF to eradicate scale insects in the affected municipalities, and the recommendations given by some volunteer groups to the PCA.;... noted however the difference in opinion of the government authorities and certain experts on the root cause of the malady, and urged the PCA and the Department of Agriculture (DA) to pinpoint the same so they can develop proper strategies for the prevention or cure of the disease.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-02-04)
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Rep. Mandanas; Interpellation by Rep. Remulla. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F002
rows.abstract:
Rep. Aggabao informed his colleagues about the
activities that transpired during the 21st Annual
Meeting of the Asia Pacific Parliamentary Forum
(APPF) recently held in Russia, which he attended
together with Reps. Rufus B. Rodriguez and Jun
Omar C. Ebdane. He also talked about the significance and relevance of the APPF as a venue for parliamentarians from the Asia-Pacific region to discuss urgent issues affecting the region and to promote regional cooperation in matters of common concern. He proposed that a House delegation must regularly and actively take part in future APPF fora.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-02-04)

rows.author: A040
rows.title_full: Effects of the Claims on the West Philippine Sea on the Rise of the Economy
rows.abstract:
As he pointed out that the situation in the West
Philippine Sea has remained fluid, Rep. Golez read portions of the following articles: Time World´s “ A Sea of Troubles: Asia Today Compared to Europe Before World War I,” which discussed the geopolitical rise of the People´s Republic of China (PROC); Xinhuanet´s “Chinese Navy Depart for West Pacific Training,” which described Chinese military capability and activity in the West Pacific; Ducky Paredes´
“The Enemy Within,” which warned about the link
between local Communist insurgency and China´s
military activities in Asia; and Bloomberg.com´s
“Consumer Boom Fuels Philippines as Asian Exports
Falter,” which highlighted the country´s thriving
economy. He thereafter prayed for peace in the region to ensure the country´s continuing economic growth and expressed hope that China would become a benign rising power.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-02-04)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Garcia (P.) and Evardone. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G097
rows.title_short: Dual Citizenship Of Those Seeking Public Office
rows.abstract:
Rep. Velasco delved into serious concerns relating to citizenship, national security concerns, and allegiance to the country by those seeking elective office, in light of the coming elections. He specifically discussed the case of Ms. Regina Ongsiako Reyes whom he alleged to have boldly tampered with and manufactured fraudulent public documents to change her identity and citizenship so she could file
her candidacy for Congress for 2013.
He opined that a renunciation of foreign citizenship under the US Immigration Act is not legally binding unless the person concerned personally appears before a US diplomatic officer and signs an oath of renunciation. He then asked the Comelec to establish screening and
document verification systems; the legislature to review inadequacies in the law; and the DFA, NSO, Comelec, and Bureau of Immigration to look into the matter.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-02-04)
